correctness.rationale: On the post-threshold spring ramp, H>0 fixes the positive square-root branch and gives the unique budburst date. For w<c put x=c−w, v=b exp(−x²/2), R=xv/√(2(h+v)). Then B′=−1+R, while B′=−1 at and beyond c (the one-sided limits agree because R(0)=0). With s=v/(h+v), (log R)_x=1/x−x(1−s/2), and s_x=−xs(1−s). Hence x²(1−s/2) increases strictly from zero to infinity; R has a unique strict peak and vanishes at both ends of x>0. Solving R=1 and R_x=0 gives v²−v−2h=0, v=y, x_c²=1+1/y, and b_c=y exp[(1+1/y)/2]. This explicit pair exists, and pointwise strict increase of R in b classifies max R below, at, or above one on the three ranges. At equality B′ vanishes only at w=c−x_c and B‴=R_xx<0 there; B″ changes sign and B is still strictly decreasing. Above equality the two x-roots are crossed in decreasing x, making the first w-turn a minimum and the second a maximum. Differentiation confirms d(log b_c)/dy=(2y−1)/(2y²)>0 and the auxiliary limits e and √(2eh). At the critical point g=log R has g_b=y/[b_c(y+1)] and g_xx=−(2y−1)/y. Rescale x−x_c by √(b−b_c); the limiting quadratic has two simple roots, yielding the stated γ and O(b−b_c) error. The finite tapered-winter integral equals x²/2 on 0≤w≤c, and c>x_+ puts both turns strictly inside it. None of this uses field validation or a rerun of the bundled checker.

value.rationale: The motivated question is whether a warming-driven advance can give way to a temporary delay and then return to advance when chilling and forcing compete. For this specified model, a numerical curve could suggest the shape but cannot certify either that no third turn is possible or exactly when the delay window first opens. The global threshold and the model-specific onset size make the switch interpretable, and the construction allows both extrema within one finite winter interval. This is useful as an exact model benchmark, not a forecast or measured tipping point.
residual_risks: No fitted species parameters or empirical two-turn evidence are available. The global continuation cannot be read as a real-season law.
